title: Greetings & politeness

grammar.title: The social glue of Darija
grammar.body:
Two words you'll hear constantly aren't just religious — they're woven into everyday speech. **l7amdulillah** ('thank God') is the normal answer to 'how are you'. **inshallah** ('God willing') stands in for the future — 'see you tomorrow, inshallah'. Using them naturally builds instant warmth.
Also: Darija drops the verb 'to be' in the present. *huwa mzyan* = 'he [is] good' — no word for 'is'.

canDo: Greet someone at any time of day and say goodbye
Ask and answer "how are you?" the way locals do
Be polite: please, thank you, excuse me

items.note: Works anytime, with anyone. Short for 'salamu 3likom'.
The fuller, warmer greeting. Reply you'll hear back: w3likom salam.
The standard reply — say it back, then ask 'w nta?' (and you?).
A heartfelt thanks you'll hear often — good to recognize.
To get past someone or apologize.
Used for anything not-yet-happened, not only in a religious sense.
